user: Her CalWORKs application was denied because her income is slightly over the limit. Which program in these documents could help with food for the baby?
reply: The Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) could help with food for the baby. SNAP provides food assistance to eligible low-income individuals and families. Source: [Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program].

user: What about early education for the 4-year-old? Which program serves preschool-age children?
reply: The Head Start program serves preschool-age children, providing comprehensive early childhood education, health, nutrition, and parent involvement services to low-income children and families. Source: [Head Start (program)].

user: Does that program also have an option for the baby?
reply: Yes, the Head Start program includes Early Head Start, which promotes healthy prenatal outcomes, healthy families, as well as infant and toddler development beginning as early as birth. Source: [Head Start (program)].

user: Is there a tax credit that could pay back part of what she spends on child care?
reply: Yes, the Child and Dependent Care Credit is a nonrefundable tax credit that could pay back part of what she spends on child care. It is available to taxpayers who incur expenses for the care of a qualifying individual, such as a child under the age of thirteen, to allow the taxpayer to be gainfully employed. The credit is a percentage of the work-related child and dependent care expenses paid to a care provider, and the percentage depends on the taxpayer’s adjusted gross income. Source: [Child and Dependent Care Credit].
